# dsh-mathtype

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that converts LaTeX placeholders in a Word `.docx`
into **real MathType OL

E objects** — `ProgID="Equation.DSMT4"`, a CFB container
holding an `Equation Native` stream — throu

gh the MathType SDK. The equations
double-click into MathType like any hand-authored one. They are n

ot Word's
built-in OMML equations and not pictures.

*Left: the `\[ ... \]` LaTeX as written in the `.docx`. Right: what Word holds
after the run — real

`Equation.DSMT4` objects, rendered here by Word itself.
The examples are textbook identities, chosen

to show the format change rather
than any one manuscript's content.*

Because the document is edited in place through Word's own automation model,
existing equation numbe

rs, `SEQ` fields, bookmarks, `REF` cross-references,
figures, tables and styles are never rebuilt.
## What it ships

One model-invocable skill, `mathtype`, registered into `ctx.skills` when the
plugin mounts:
| Path | Role |

| `mt_env.py` | Discovers MathType, `MT6.dll`, Word and Python deps; smoke-tests the SDK. |
| `mt_sd

k.py` | `MT6.dll` wrapper: connect, `set_latex`, `get_text`, close. |
| `mt_prefs.py` | Equation siz

e via the MathType registry block, restored afterwards. |
| `word_session.py` | Word session that su

rvives RPC crashes and late-binding failures. |
| `convert_docx.py` | The conversion. `--dry-run`, `

--overrides`, `--report`. |
| `verify_docx.py` | Structural proof: ProgID, CFB, `Equation Native`, r

els, ShapeID, bookmarks, fields. |
| `render_check.py` | Export PDF, render page and per-equation QA

sheets. |
| `make_fixture.py` | Build a 6-equation test document with real `SEQ` fields. |

No JavaScript dependencies: the registrar uses only `node:fs`, `node:path` and
`node:url`, so the pa
ckage installs offline.
## Requirements
| Component | Requirement |

| OS | Windows 10/11. COM and OLE have no macOS or Linux equivalent. |
| MathType | MathType 7 deskt

op, **full install** — the fonts-only package has no `System\<arch>\MT6.dll`. |
| Word | Desktop Wor

d 2016/2019/2021/365. Not a viewer, not LibreOffice. |
| Python | 3.10+, bitness matching `MT6.dll`

(64-bit Python ↔ `System\64\MT6.dll`). |
| Python packages | `pywin32`, `lxml`. Optional: `pymupdf`
+ `Pillow` for the render check. |
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Nothing is hard-coded: the MathType directory, SDK DLL and preference files are
resolved from the re
gistry at run time, so a non-default install location works.

e chain with the bundled fixture first

## Use
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Recognised placeholders, one per paragraph:
| Source | Result |

| `\[a=b\tag{7}\]` | centred MathType object, number `(7)` right-aligned |
| `\[a=b\tag{2a}\]` | num

ber `(2a)`; sub-lettering survives |
| `\[a=b\]` | centred object, no number |
| `$a=b$` | inline ob

2a)`; sub-lettering survives |
| `\[a=b\]` | centred object, no number |
| `$a=b$` | inline object |

Numbers inside `\tag{...}` are never regenerated: an existing `SEQ` field,
bookmark or literal `2a`
is kept verbatim, so every `REF` still resolves.

`--size` sets the equation size (accepts `10.5` or `"10.5 pt"`); the previous
MathType setting is re

stored afterwards. `--align none` leaves paragraph layout
untouched. `--overrides fixes.json` replac
es individual equations by label.
## Limitations

- Windows only.
- It converts existing LaTeX placeholders; it does not author or validate
mathematic

s.
- It does not convert MathType back to LaTeX in batch (the SDK wrapper exposes
`get_text()` for s

ingle equations).
- It does not produce Word OMML — that is the other direction.
- Requires the real

MathType installation; the SDK DLL is never redistributed
with this plugin.
